No FiniteDimensional instance is a hidden premise: the given finite basis supplies finite-dimensionality when subsequently needed. judgment.application: There are two uses in /proof. After B102, the original integer basis is also a complex basis of the original finite-dimensional V; after establishing finiteness and indexing it by Fin m, B005 over C gives finrank_C V=m. The original dimension l+1 then gives m=l+1 and permits reindexing the original integer basis. In B103, B002 gives a K-basis indexed by Fin(l+1), so B005 gives dim_K N=l+1, furnishing B105's dimension hypothesis. These uses do not assume a specially recovered lattice basis and do not infer the size of an arbitrary infinite basis by using the finite-index theorem backwards.

The original dimension l+1 then gives m=l+1 and permits reindexing the original integer basis. In B103, B002 gives a K-basis indexed by Fin(l+1), so B005 gives dim_K N=l+1, furnishing B105's dimension hypothesis. These uses do not assume a specially recovered lattice basis and do not infer the size of an arbitrary infinite basis by using the finite-index theorem backwards.
